speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what have been the changes in the number of products certified under the Singapore Green Labelling Scheme in the past three years; and (b)what will the Ministry do to promote more companies to have more green-labelled products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: SEC's SGLS is one of the several green labelling schemes in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As a major buyer of goods and services, the public sector plays a role in encouraging companies to provide greener products and services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The public sector regularly reviews and updates its green procurement policies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We hope that this will spur companies to produce, develop or supply more green products and services.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the very comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Essentially, it is good for environment, but it must also be something that is available in the market readily and at a price point that makes sense for such commercial decisions.
